Q: ansifilter doesn't filter ANSI escape codes A:

\r move cursor to start of the line

\n new line (and with some console setups, imply move cursor to the start of the line)

Try to use either \n or \r\n instead of \r

Q: Trying to get VS Editor with Python to run pytest A:

This usually happens because of pytest, even if Python is installed.exe is not genuinely in the PATH that terminal you are using is utilizing.

Here are a few things I would check:

Step 1. Firstly verify Python is working or not: In Powershell type python --version or py --version

Step 2. Check if pytest is installed or not: Type python -m pip show pytest

Step 3. Instead of running: pytest try python -m pytest or py -m pytest. This is the suggested method of running pytest and gets around PATH problems.

Step 4. If python -m pytest runs but pytest fails, then your Scripts directory is not on your PATH. It should usually look something like:

C:\Users<YourUser>\AppData\Local\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64\Scripts

Restart Visual Studio Code and launch a new terminal after adding it.

Step 5. Also, make sure VS Code uses the exact same Python interpreter as pytest. You may check this in Python by selecting Interpreter in the Command Palette.

Since you are implementing Python 3.14, it is also well worth confirming you are employing the official installer as well as not a various distribution that retains packages in an unusual location. Running python -m pytest --version will swiftly tell you whether Python can actually find pytest.

If python -m pytest works, then it is almost certainly just a PATH configuration issue rather than a problem with pytest itself.
